name: SHIDO permissionless V1-to-V2 migration arbitrage
summary: ShidoLock.lockTokens()/claimTokens() swap SHIDO V1 for V2 one to one for any caller, with no snapshot of pre-migration holders, while V1 traded about twenty times cheaper. The attacker flash-borrowed WBNB, bought 10.4B V1 from its thin pool, locked it, claimed 10.4B V2 out of the reward wallet's approved balance and sold the V2 into the V2/WBNB pool.
notes: claimTokens() pays V2 by transferFrom from the reward wallet, so the wallet's unlimited V2 approval to ShidoLock, given about 1,000 blocks after deployment, is a custody grant the exploit needed and sets the reset (rule 8).

Loss is the WBNB the V2/WBNB pool paid for the claimed V2 (its realised value, as V2 is unpriced). The 39.1 WBNB the attacker spent on V1 and its flash loan are not netted. No earlier or later claim of comparable size: the next largest pre-exploit claims were under 0.8B V2 by ordinary holders, and claims stopped soon after.
